History:
- Main complaint: Lower abdominal pain for the last 2 days.
- Characteristics: Central lower abdominal pain, feels hot and sweaty.
- Associated symptoms: Slight nausea, no vomiting, increased thirst, feeling sweaty, slight pink blood in urine.
- Bowel: History of constipation last week, now normal. No blood in stool.
- Urinary: Increased frequency of urination, no dysuria, no strong urine smell, no back pain.
- No recent travel. No prior similar episodes.
- Menstrual: Regular periods, no intermenstrual or post-coital bleeding, no abnormal discharge.
- No recent shivering; measured temperature ~37°C one hour ago, not elevated.
- Social: Lives with parents. Drinks alcohol (~1 beer, 4 times per week). Does not smoke.
- Family history: Mother had breast cancer (treated early).

Past Medical History:
- No significant chronic illnesses or prior hospitalizations reported.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.
- Medications: No regular or OTC medications. Previously used internal contraceptive implant for one year; no longer in use.
- No other allergies or medication intolerances reported.

Physical Examination:
- No documented physical exam findings.
- Patient reports: No back pain, no abdominal pain radiating, no throat swelling, no strong urine odor, no vomiting, no abnormal discharge, alert and oriented.

Impression:
- Suspected urinary tract infection (UTI).

Management Plan:
- Prescribed 3-day course of antibiotics (name and dose/route/frequency not documented; instructed to take twice daily).
- Instructions to initiate antibiotics as soon as possible.
- Advised to contact clinic if symptoms worsen (increasing pain, high temperature, new symptoms, or back pain) or if recurrent symptoms develop.
- Advise face-to-face review if deterioration occurs.

Patient Summary:
- Patient presented with new-onset lower abdominal pain and urinary symptoms. UTI suspected; prescribed antibiotics and instructed regarding warning symptoms and follow-up. Will monitor response to prescribed treatment.

Key Takeaways:
- Start prescribed antibiotics promptly and complete full course.
- Seek urgent re-assessment if pain worsens, fever, back pain, or new symptoms arise.
- Contact clinic if symptoms do not improve or recur.

Next Steps:
- Collect antibiotics from pharmacy and begin treatment.
- Monitor for progression or new symptoms.
- Arrange further medical review if condition deteriorates or does not improve.
